name: Fionnghal nam Fiadh

attributes.attribute: also called Flora of the Deer
wild woman of an Irish tale
went mad when her lover left
grew from the graves and entwined

sources: Carmichael, Alexander. Carmina Gadelica: Hymns and Incantations. Hudson, N.Y.: Lindisfarne Press, 1992, 657.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fionnghal nam Fiadh was a Scottish heroine whose names include Flora of the Deer and the Crazed One, a wild woman of the mountains. Her story echoes the tale of Mis, the wild woman of Ireland. Fionnghal was a beautiful maiden. Her lover jilted her and married a richer woman on his mother's advice. Madness seized Fionnghal, and she fled naked and screaming into the mountains. Among the deer she made her home, growing hair until she looked like one of the herd, and the deer took her for their own. Her kinsmen gave up the chase, but her former lover kept tracking her. One day he found her sleeping naked at his own camp. He laid his cloak over her and stayed. She woke sane and grateful, told him she was dying, and soon died. He carried her body down from the mountains, delivered it to her kin, and died himself. From the pair of graves two tall weeping willows rose and twined together.
